questions.text: According to Western wedding folklore, what action is a bride supposed to take to bring good luck to an unmarried woman?
options: She blows out the candles on a cake
She tosses her bouquet over her shoulder
She opens a gift from her mother
questions.explanation: In many folk traditions, a bride throwing her bouquet over her shoulder is believed to bring good luck to the single woman who catches it, symbolizing that she will be next to marry.

questions.text: In Scandinavian folklore, what small, bearded creature is traditionally said to protect a farm and its inhabitants from misfortune?
questions.explanation: The nisse is a tomte-like creature from Scandinavian folklore, typically associated with homesteads and barns.

questions.text: In medieval Germanic folklore, during which seasonal period was the spectral 'Wild Hunt' most commonly said to ride?
questions.explanation: In old European folklore, particularly from the Rhineland and Germanic regions, the 'wild hunt' was most often led by the god Woden (Odin) during the Yule season, not during the autumn equinox or midsummer night.
